transcript: The thing about Oliver that surprised me is it wasn't just during the encore and the bows. Now, I've never been to a panto, and I know that's a very different experience. I've seen a lot of shows in London and the audiences just seem to be a little quieter. This is not a theater etiquette thing. This is just like, less reactions. I don't want to get into theater etiquette, it's just a cultural difference. But for Oliver, people were so engaged the entire time, during every big number. Food, Glorious Food. I'll do anything. Oompa PA, consider yourself. People were hyped like they do consider yourself. And then there's a full reprise where they're all turning to the audience dodgers, like standing on a table and like, having everyone singing clap along. I've never seen that in London. Again, haven't been to a panto, but everyone was like, losing it. They were so excited. And don't get me wrong, I loved it. I thought it was so fun cause I just had never seen that in London before. I do think it's funny because as an American who, like, did not grow up in the Oliver Laura that is clearly like so ingrained in the UK. Oliver is like, really dark and really sad. Like, spoiler, I guess Nancy gets brutally unalived by her boyfriend on stage. And yet people think Oliver is basically like British Annie. But anyway, this production is exceptional. Like, it is big and Bold. And if you see one production of Oliver in your life, this is the one to see.
